title: Provenance Semirings
abstract: Introduces a general algebraic framework in which provenance annotations are propagated through relational queries. The representation provides transfer foundations for compositional lineage of derived values, although its empirical domain is relational data rather than versioned multimodal documents.
venue: ACM Symposium on Principles of Database Systems (PODS 2007)

admission.reason: The paper is foundational provenance theory, but the supplied abstract describes an algebraic annotation framework rather than an empirical method for versioned multimodal documents or an evaluated workplace-like provenance task. For this round's direct empirical focus, the more concrete lineage-tracing candidate materially strengthens TF11 with less transfer distance.

title: Dual Attention Networks for Visual Reference Resolution in Visual Dialog
abstract: Models visual reference resolution in dialogue with dedicated mechanisms for finding and referring to visually grounded entities. The method is empirically evaluated in visual-dialog settings and serves as transfer evidence for multimodal referring-expression grounding.

admission.reason: The abstract shows visual reference resolution in visual dialogue, but this capability substantially overlaps the admitted GRAVL-BERT and J-CRe3 candidates. It does not add a more document-like target, attachment/version grounding, or a distinctive failure/evaluation dimension that justifies another reading slot.

title: Visual Grounding for User Interfaces
abstract: Takes a user-interface screenshot together with a free-form referring expression and identifies the interface element denoted by that expression. The method incorporates layout information and is empirically evaluated on screenshot grounding, making it structurally close transfer evidence for references such as highlighted or nearby screen regions.

admission.reason: The abstract shows free-form expression grounding to GUI elements and is relevant to TF18, but its contribution is substantially duplicated by VERIFIED candidates Ferret-UI and Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents. Because its identity is UNCHECKED and the supplied abstract does not establish a uniquely stronger document-like capability, it does not merit an additional reading slot.

title: Extracting implicit tree structures in spreadsheet calculation
abstract: Empirically studies how implicit computational structures are extracted from spreadsheet calculations. Experiments involving multiple spreadsheet types provide early evidence that spreadsheet computations possess higher-level hierarchical organization beyond individual cells.

admission.reason: The abstract establishes that spreadsheet calculations can exhibit higher-level implicit structure, but it does not show workbook-level semantic reconstruction, explicit formula dependency provenance, cross-sheet relationships, version lineage, or the structural features named in gap-3. The topic is adjacent but the demonstrated capability is too limited.

title: Reference Resolution and Context Change in Multimodal Situated Dialogue for Exploring Data Visualizations
abstract: Empirically studies reference resolution in multimodal dialogue where people discuss data visualizations while also using gestures. The work models how referring expressions establish or revisit visual entities and supplies structurally relevant transfer evidence for grounding workplace references into visual regions.

admission.reason: The abstract provides relevant multimodal reference-resolution evidence over data visualizations and gestures, but that transfer mechanism is already covered more directly by the admitted conversational/coreference and GUI-grounding candidates. It does not add attachment identity, page/cell localization, or version grounding.

title: Multi-modal Reference Resolution in Situated Dialogue by Integrating Linguistic and Extra-Linguistic Clues
abstract: Combines linguistic context with extra-linguistic visual information for resolving references in situated dialogue. The empirical task requires linking referring expressions to entities in the shared visual environment, making it transfer evidence for attachment-region reference resolution.

admission.reason: The abstract demonstrates multimodal reference resolution by combining linguistic and visual clues, but this mechanism is substantially duplicated by the admitted J-CRe3 and GRAVL-BERT candidates. It does not add a more document-specific target, explicit attachment/version identity, or a distinctive localization granularity.

title: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
abstract: Trains a vision-language model to ground natural-language instructions directly to locations in GUI screenshots and introduces evaluation for GUI grounding. Although the surface is an interactive interface rather than a workplace attachment, the task directly tests expression-to-screen-region localization.

admission.reason: SeeClick directly grounds instructions to GUI screenshot locations, but this capability is already represented by the admitted VERIFIED Ferret-UI and Universal Visual Grounding candidates. The supplied abstract does not show a distinctive discourse, version, or document-structure contribution that warrants another transfer reading slot.

title: Matching document images with ground truth
abstract: Develops methods for aligning document images with electronic ground-truth representations so that source information can be associated with positions in scanned images. The work is an early document-image alignment foundation for transferring logical or textual annotations to image coordinates.
venue: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition

admission.reason: The paper aligns scanned document images with electronic ground-truth representations so annotations can be associated with image positions. That is useful historical document-image registration, but it is not successive-version element correspondence or semantic change detection, and the newer admitted TF1 candidates address the target capability more directly.

title: Semi-structured document image matching and recognition
abstract: Studies matching, recognition, and localization of semi-structured document images using techniques adapted from visual object recognition. The method addresses repeated textual patterns and variable layouts, making it relevant transfer evidence for document-region correspondence.

admission.reason: The abstract concerns matching and localizing semi-structured document images under layout variability, but it does not establish revision lineage, persistent element identity, or explicit change classification. Its correspondence capability is weaker and less directly version-oriented than the admitted paragraph-alignment and region-matching papers.

title: Flow-Based Page Unique Semantic Mapping Architecture for Document Visual Question Answering
abstract: Introduces FUMA for distinguishing semantically similar document pages and localizing evidence through question-conditioned page representations and reversible flow-based mappings. Experiments evaluate both evidence localization and answer generation, but the localized unit is primarily the page rather than a complete page-region-cell hierarchy.

admission.reason: FUMA evaluates page-level evidence localization and answer generation, but its primary localized unit is the page. The admitted VERIFIED multi-page DocVQA candidates already cover page routing and long-document evidence selection, and this unchecked candidate does not close the page-region-cell hierarchy required by gap-4.
